title: Climbing Stairs
description:
A staircase has `n` steps. From any position you can climb either **1** or **2** steps at a time.

Return the number of distinct ways to reach the top.
hints: The last move onto step n came from step n-1 or step n-2.
So ways(n) = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2): the Fibonacci recurrence with ways(1) = 1, ways(2) = 2.
Two rolling variables are enough; no array needed.
approach:
**The number of ways to stand on step `i` is the sum of the ways to stand on the two steps you could have come from.** `ways(i) = ways(i-1) + ways(i-2)`, with `ways(0) = ways(1) = 1`. That is the Fibonacci sequence shifted by one.

Naive recursion recomputes the same subproblems and is O(2^n); n = 45 already takes minutes. Memoising or iterating bottom-up makes it O(n). Since each state only depends on the previous two, **two rolling variables** give O(1) space, which is the version to present.

**Common mistakes:** off-by-one at the base cases (ways(2) must be 2), and starting the loop at the wrong index so that n = 1 returns 2.

**Interview follow-ups:** Allow steps of size 1..k? (Sum the previous k values with a sliding window sum.) Enumerate the actual sequences rather than count them? (Backtracking; the output itself is exponential.) Compute in O(log n)? (Fast matrix exponentiation of [[1,1],[1,0]].) Forbidden steps? (Set ways(i) = 0 for broken steps.)
